gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the eufy 4G LTE Cam S330 pairs with a HomeBase only in Wi-Fi mode, so on cellular it records to microSD alone and HomeBase 2 is not supported at all, or that Reolink's 4G cameras such as the Go PT Ultra cannot be added to a Reolink Home Hub.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. Buffalo Alarm (buffaloalarm.com/recommended-products/cellular-security-cameras) names the S330 and Go PT Ultra but says nothing about HomeBase or Home Hub pairing, firmware, LTE bands or region versions, and claims 'Most cellular cameras work with all major carriers.' Reolink's 4G solar guide (reolink.com/blog/4g-solar-security-cameras-buying-guide) already gives the US LTE bands and says the bundled SIM uses AT&T, Verizon or T-Mobile, so bands are not new. It does not mention the Home Hub exclusion for 4G cameras. It also omits that the Go PT Ultra product page recommends only T-Mobile or AT&T prepaid data-only SIMs if you bring your own. I did not open the uncited top results (securitycamhq, securitycamlab, smarthomeexplorer and others), so they may cover part of this.
decides: It confirms that both top picks are standalone cellular cameras. Neither one gets local hub backup while it runs on LTE: eufy pairs with a HomeBase only over Wi-Fi, and Reolink's Home Hub does not support 4G cameras. A buyer who wants a hub at a remote site should not count on it, and the microSD card is the only local copy. The S330 is still the right pick for a site that sometimes has Wi-Fi, because there it can join a HomeBase S380, mini or Professional S1. It cannot join a HomeBase 2. For a bring-your-own SIM, Reolink names T-Mobile or AT&T prepaid data-only, while eufy's bundled EIOTCLUB SIM also uses Verizon. Both SIMs are tied to the region where you bought the camera, and the US bands are B2/B4/B5/B12/B13/B14/B66/B71. EU and Australian Reolink units use different bands, so a gray-import unit is a bad buy.

findings.label: HomeBase S380 (HomeBase 3) compatibility
findings.note: The table row for 4G LTE Cam S330 / T86P2 reads 'Compatible (only under Wi-Fi mode)'. On the same page, the cellular-only 4G Starlight Cam S230 is 'Not Compatible' because it 'operates via cellular signal and does not connect to Wi-Fi'.

findings.label: Supported HomeBases and exclusion
findings.value: HomeBase S380, HomeBase Professional S1 and HomeBase mini over Wi-Fi only; HomeBase 2 not supported
findings.note: Quote: 'It can also connect to HomeBase S380 (HomeBase 3), HomeBase Professional S1, or HomeBase mini over Wi-Fi … while HomeBase 2 is not supported.' Clips go 'to the microSD card or, on Wi-Fi, to a connected HomeBase.' The page's spec table lists only 'HomeBase S380 / HomeBase mini (not HomeBase 2)', which conflicts with the FAQ on Professional S1. Also states: no Apple HomeKit, no NAS storage, no cross-camera tracking, Wi-Fi on 2.4 GHz only.

findings.label: Included SIM carriers and US LTE bands
findings.value: EIOTCLUB 3-in-1 nano SIM on AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon; US bands B2/B4/B5/B12/B13/B14/B66/B71
findings.note: Quote: 'The included EIOTCLUB 3-in-1 nano SIM runs on AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon.' The camera picks the strongest of the three. The SIM comes with 100 MB of trial data for 7 days. You can use your own nano SIM 'with a data-only plan' after checking with the provider.

findings.label: Region limit on the bundled SIM

findings.note: Quote: 'The SIM is intended for the region where the camera was purchased, so using it abroad may stop it from connecting.'

findings.note: The article says '4G cameras are Not Supported' but does not name the Go PT Ultra. I am treating the Go PT Ultra as covered because its product page says 'The camera does not support WiFi connection' and connects over 4G LTE only.

findings.product: Reolink Go PT Ultra (Go Series G440)
findings.label: Carriers recommended for your own SIM
findings.value: US: T-Mobile (prepaid data only), AT&T (prepaid data only); MVNOs FreedomPop, Mint
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra product page
findings.note: Quote: 'We recommend T-Mobile (prepaid data only) if you are in the U.S.' Verizon is not on the recommended list for your own SIM. The bundled SIM 'allows the camera to automatically connect to the strongest available network from A&T [sic], Verizon, or T-Mobile (US).' The page also says 'The camera does not supports 5G or 2G SIM card', recommends against 3G, and requires a nano SIM dedicated to the camera.

findings.product: Reolink Go PT Ultra (Go Series G440)
findings.label: LTE bands by regional version
findings.value: USA LTE FDD B2/B4/B5/B12/B13/B14/B66/B71; Europe B1/B3/B7/B8/B20/B28A plus WCDMA B1/B8; Australia B1/B3/B5/B7/B8/B28 plus WCDMA B1/B5/B8
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra product page
findings.note: The EU and AU versions lack US bands B2, B4, B12, B13, B14, B66 and B71, so imported units are poor matches for US carriers. My inference from band overlap: an EU unit shares only B5 with the US band list if it is the AU version, and shares no US band if it is the EU version.

findings.note: The box list has no panel. The page offers '6W Reolink Solar Panel 2*', but its footnote text does not appear on the page. Reolink's US cellular page (https://store.reolink.com/us/cellular-security-camera/, read 2026-11-13) lists the Go PT Ultra as 'Solar Panel 2 compatible'. Reolink's panel article (https://support.reolink.com/articles/900000593886-Which-Cameras-Can-Work-with-Reolink-Solar-Panel/) lists the Go PT Ultra in its 'Solar Panel (3W)' recommendation group and says Solar Panel 2 (6W) could work with all battery cameras except Argus, Keen and Doorbell (Battery). The page extraction there was ambiguous about group headings.
